title: In a 21-site field test, 38 percent of heat pump installs needed a new electrical panel

scenes.purpose: Land the one figure the Short exists for, with its denominator named above it, and leave the viewer holding the question.

visual.description: Portrait frame, the institution's ground. A single ledger tile sits centred in the content band with the accent rule down its left edge; above it the small muted line '21 heat pump installs'. The figure counts up to 38% on the word 'thirty-eight' and holds; the label 'Needed a new panel' fades in beneath it. Nothing else moves while the question is spoken, so the tile is still on screen as the viewer hears 'Was it in your quote?'.

chart.title: 21 heat pump installs
chart.note: The share of the field test's sites, read from the installers' invoices; not a national rate.

scenes.direction: Cold open, no intro: the title line is already set when the first word lands. Tile counts up on 'thirty-eight' and holds. Hold the full tile, unchanged, through 'Was it in your quote?' — the question is the beat, not a new graphic.
scenes.narration: Across 21 heat pump installs, 38 percent needed a new electrical panel. Was it in your quote?

scenes.purpose: Take the 38 percent away from the viewer's own house immediately: name the population in type, so the qualification is seen as well as heard.

visual.description: The tile clears. Three ruled lines build down the content band, one as its words are spoken: 'Cold-climate prototypes', then 'A field test', then 'Not a national survey'. Each earlier line dims as the next arrives. The last clause, that the share is not the odds for your house, is carried by the captions the video draws; no fourth line.

scenes.direction: Hard cut from the tile. Each line enters on its own words ('cold-climate prototypes', 'field test', 'national survey'). Hold all three while 'not the odds for your house' is spoken.
scenes.narration: Those were cold-climate prototypes in a field test, not a national survey, so that share is not the odds for your house.

scenes.purpose: Give the cost of the electrical work as what the record gives it as: a range across the sites that needed it, for labour and materials only.

visual.description: Two ledger tiles stacked in the content band under the muted line 'Electrical upgrades': $3,750 above, $8,970 below, each with the accent rule. The upper tile counts up on the first figure, the lower on the second, so the range is read as two observed ends rather than one price. Both hold while 'before the heat pump itself' is spoken.

chart.title: Electrical upgrades
chart.note: Labour and materials for a site's electrical upgrades entire, where upgrades were needed; the heat pump itself is not in it, and this is not the price of a panel.

scenes.direction: Tiles land on their own figures. 'Lowest site' and 'Highest site' are labels the narration does not speak: let each fade in a beat after its figure has settled, so the range reads as observed ends. Hold both to the end of the sentence.
scenes.narration: Where electrical upgrades were needed, they alone ran $3,750 to $8,970 in labour and materials, before the heat pump itself.

scenes.purpose: Show the panel-only figure in the record's own sentence, with its attribution visible, so it is read as one item and a cited estimate rather than as the small end of the previous range.

visual.description: The tiles clear to a paper card filling the content band: the document and line numbers in small mono at the top, the passage set in the serif beneath. The sentence 'The typical cost for a 200 amp electrical panel upgrade is $1,954 (Lane, 2019)' underlines in the accent as it is spoken, carrying '(Lane, 2019)' inside the highlight so the viewer sees whose estimate it is and what year it is from. The words that follow in the same passage, about the cost of each dedicated circuit, stay visible unhighlighted as 'plus wiring for each new circuit' is said. No tile, no comparison with the previous scene.

excerpt.highlight: The typical cost for a 200 amp electrical panel upgrade is $1,954 (Lane, 2019)

scenes.direction: Cut to the card on 'For a 200-amp panel'. Highlight draws across the sentence as it is spoken and holds. Nothing from sc03 is on screen: the two figures are never framed side by side.
scenes.narration: For a 200-amp panel on its own, a retrofit cost report cites an outside estimate of $1,954, plus wiring for each new circuit.

scenes.purpose: Hand the viewer to the full inquiry; the video draws this as the end card.

visual.description: End card drawn by the video: the institution's seal, the full inquiry's question and the call to action. No lines of its own.

scenes.direction: Dissolve from the paper card to the end card. Hold to the last word and a beat after.
scenes.narration: What the whole install really costs is the question the full inquiry takes on.
